title: Bimodal rolling–flying robot
description: A quadrotor with passive wheels uses its existing propellers for flight and surface locomotion.
introduction: Flight helps a robot reach an inspection site, while rolling can keep it close to a surface without continuously supporting its weight in the air. This robot combines those capabilities using passive wheels and a shared propulsion system.

problem.heading: Inspection does not always require continuous flight.
paragraphs: A small aerial robot can reach surfaces that are difficult to access from the ground. Once there, maintaining contact or travelling along the surface presents a different locomotion problem from free flight.

Adding a separate powered ground drivetrain increases the number of actuators and mechanisms the vehicle must carry. The research asks how one propulsion system can support both aerial access and surface motion.

approach.heading: One propulsion system, two ways to move.
paragraphs: Two passive wheels support the quadrotor during surface locomotion. The propellers provide the forces needed to move along flat or inclined surfaces, while the same vehicle retains its flight capability.

The design connects platform mechanics with motion control: thrust must be used differently when the wheels constrain the robot than when the robot is freely flying. The published study addresses this rolling–flying configuration for close inspection.

evidence.label: Physical prototype
evidence.text: The supplied experiments demonstrate propeller-driven rolling, ramp motion and the platform’s surface/flight capabilities. These are genuine prototype tests.

evidence.label: Scope of the demonstrations
evidence.text: The clips illustrate particular operating conditions. They do not establish a universal energy saving or mission endurance multiplier.
